root_directory.description: Firebird installation root; the tree under this path holds bin/, lib/, plugins/, and include/

remote_service_port.description: TCP port Firebird listens on for client connections (IANA-assigned default is 3050)

remote_bind_address.description: IP address to bind to; leave empty to accept connections on all interfaces

remote_aux_port.description: Auxiliary port for async event delivery; 0 lets the OS assign a free ephemeral port

max_connections.description: Maximum simultaneous database attachments across the entire server instance; 0 = unlimited

connection_timeout.description: Seconds of inactivity before an idle client connection is dropped; 0 = never drop

dummy_packet_interval.description: Interval in seconds between keepalive dummy packets sent to clients to prevent stateful-firewall drops

auth_server.description: Server-side authentication plugins tried in order; valid names: Srp256, Srp, Legacy_Auth, Win_Sspi

plugin_name.description: Authentication plugin name (e.g. Srp256, Srp, Legacy_Auth)

auth_client.description: Client-side authentication plugins offered to the server; order determines preference

plugin_name.description: Authentication plugin name (e.g. Srp256, Srp, Legacy_Auth)

user_manager.description: Plugin that manages Firebird user accounts; use Srp for modern installs, Legacy_UserManager only for Firebird 2.x compatibility

wire_crypt.description: Wire encryption: Required = always enforce TLS-like encryption, Enabled = honour client request, Disabled = plaintext only

security_database.description: Absolute path to the Firebird security database (security4.fdb) that stores user credentials and roles

server_mode.description: Server architecture: SuperServer is best for most workloads; SuperClassic improves SMP throughput; Classic gives maximum isolation at higher process overhead

max_parallel_workers.description: Maximum intra-query parallel worker threads (SuperServer only); 1 disables parallelism; set to logical CPU count for analytics workloads

default_db_cache_pages.description: Default number of page-cache buffers per database (each page is 4–16 KB); larger values reduce I/O at the cost of RAM

file_system_cache_threshold.description: Database size in pages above which Firebird switches to direct I/O (O_DIRECT) bypassing the OS page cache; lower values reduce double-buffering on large databases

file_system_cache_size.description: Maximum percentage of physical RAM the OS file cache may use for Firebird files; 0 leaves the decision to the OS

temp_cache_limit.description: Maximum in-memory temporary workspace in bytes before sort/merge data spills to disk; default 64 MB (67108864); increase for heavy OLAP queries

temp_directories.description: Directories for on-disk temporary sort/merge files; empty list = use the OS default temp dir; entries are joined with semicolons in the config

path.description: Absolute path to a directory writable by the firebird OS user

max_unflushed_writes.description: Maximum pending page writes before Firebird forces a disk flush; -1 = no limit (OS-controlled); lower values improve durability at the cost of write throughput

max_unflushed_write_time.description: Maximum seconds pending writes may stay unflushed before a forced flush; -1 = no time limit

gc_policy.description: Garbage collection strategy: combined (cooperative + background, recommended), cooperative, background, or none

database_access.description: Controls which database files the server may open: Full, None, or Restrict followed by a semicolon-separated list of allowed paths

external_file_access.description: Controls access to external table data files: None (most secure, recommended), Full, or Restrict <path-list>

udf_access.description: Controls loading of legacy UDF shared libraries: None (recommended — prefer UDR in Firebird 4.0), Full, or Restrict <path-list>

audit_trace_config_file.description: Absolute path to the audit trace config file; empty string disables server-level audit logging entirely

data_type_compatibility.description: Compatibility level for legacy clients: '3.0' restores Firebird 3.0 type semantics for VARCHAR/NUMERIC/TIME columns; leave empty for native Firebird 4.0 behaviour
